newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian mint wins euro bill design competition.
newsitem.headline: Austrian mint wins euro bill design competition.

text.p: When Europeans reach into their pockets for the new euro bills in 1999, what they will retrieve will be designed by artists at the Austrian mint, the country's central bank said on Friday.
The bank's designers won a Europe-wide competition to determine the face of the seven new bills, in denominations of between five and 500 euros.
"This is it -- that's what the new euro will look like," a central bank spokeswoman said. "All that remains to be done is to add in some safety features."
The brightly-coloured notes depict a stylised map of Europe on one side, and various architectural motifs such as bridges, windows and arches on the other.
The designs represent "openness and cooperation between the European states", the bank said. "The notes symbolise the advent of a new, unified Europe and a common European future."
The Austrian proposal was chosen by a panel of 14 experts after some 2,000 citizens from across the union were asked to comment on the ten front runners.

Production of the notes will start at printing plants across the continent in 1998 once they have been signed by the future president of the European central bank. They will be brought into circulation by January 1, 2002.
